value.first: I'd use the Ferber method (graduated check-ins). It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and the skill it teaches - falling asleep alone at bedtime - is the same one he needs to get back down at 3am. Start on a clear week: same bedtime, same 20-30 min routine, feed before the book, then into the crib drowsy but awake and leave. If you can't stand timed crying, the chair method is the gentler, slower version.
value.second: Nights 1-3: when he cries, wait 3 min, then 5, then 10 for every check after. Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15. Checks are 1-2 min, lights off, same short phrase, then leave - no pickup, no feed. At 3am, restart that night's sequence from its first wait. Expect 30-60+ min of protest and a worse night 2 or 3 - that's the old pattern breaking. Decide ahead which parent does checks.
value.third: Nights 4-7: Night 4: 12/15/17. Night 5: 15/17/20. Night 6: 17/20/25. Night 7: 20/25/30. It's working when he settles faster and the 3am waking shortens or stops. If he snores, gasps, or pauses breathing in his sleep, that's worth a doctor's look - no method fixes that. I'll check in Thursday.
